record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Turn ISS theory into systematic robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional systems and PDEs. More concretely, develop practical ISS-based design methods for boundary or distributed robust controllers across important application areas where robust control design remains largely open.

evidence.quote: 10.4. Robust control design. As it has been already explained, the Lyapunov approach is useful for ISS analysis of PDE systems and for the design of boundary controllers ensuring an ISS property of the closed-loop system.

Many open control problems exist in the literature for robust control designs, as the drilling problem (see [193] and references therein), and the flexible structure control in aircraft (see in particular [60, 189]) to point out only a few robust control problems. Use of ISS techniques for robust control design is, to a large extent, still an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional control systems—particularly those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs)—based on the framework of input-to-state stability (ISS).

Setup and definitions. Consider a control system of the form
  ẋ(t) = A x(t) + f(x(t), u(t), d(t)),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach (or Hilbert) state space, A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on X (or, more generally, the dynamics are described by an evolution equation on X possibly with unbounded boundary input operators), u(·) takes values in a control space U, and d(·) ∈ L^∞(ℝ₊; D) represents an exogenous disturbance taking values in a normed space D. Boundary control is allowed: inputs may enter through boundary conditions of the underlying PDE.

The closed-loop system under a feedback law u = K(x) is said to be input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to the disturbance d if there exist a class-KL function β and a class-K function γ such that, for every x₀ ∈ X and every admissible d,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖d‖_{L^∞(0,t;D)})  for all t ≥ 0.

Problem. Provide a constructive design framework that, given a class of PDE control systems (for example, parabolic or hyperbolic PDEs in one or several space dimensions, with either distributed or boundary actuation), produces feedback laws K—possibly together with ISS-Lyapunov functionals certifying the closed-loop ISS estimate above—and that is general enough to address concrete robust control problems in which a systematic methodology is currently lacking, such as:
  (a) the drilling problem (axial/torsional vibrations modeled by wave equations with nonlinear boundary conditions);
  (b) robust stabilization of flexible aircraft structures (beam/plate equations coupled with rigid-body dynamics and uncertain aerodynamic loads).

The methodology should specify (i) the admissible classes of disturbances and uncertainties, (ii) the construction of ISS-Lyapunov functionals for the closed loop, (iii) verifiable sufficient conditions on the controller gains ensuring the desired ISS gain γ, and (iv) extensions to cases with unbounded input operators arising from boundary actuation.
artifact.category_tag: Input-to-state stability and robust control of PDEs
artifact.status_search_result: The development of a systematic ISS-based robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional and PDE systems is recognized as a broad open research direction. While Lyapunov-based ISS analysis and small-gain results have advanced (e.g., for ODE-PDE interconnections and networks of infinite-dimensional systems), no comprehensive constructive design framework covering the cited application areas (drilling, flexible aircraft structures) has been established. Recent surveys and tutorials (2020–2021) continue to list robust ISS-based design as an active and largely open problem.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems: Recent Results and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Pedagogical survey of ISS for infinite-dimensional systems listing robust control design as a largely open direction.
status_evidence.claim: Robust control design via ISS techniques for infinite-dimensional systems is highlighted as still largely open.

status_evidence.title: ECC21 Tutorial Session on Stability and robust control of PDEs
status_evidence.snippet: Tutorial on stability and robust control of PDEs and large-scale systems, indicating active ongoing research without a unified design framework.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2021, robust control of PDEs based on ISS remains an active research area with no unified methodology.

status_evidence.title: Robust Stability of a Nonlinear ODE-PDE System
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes ISS for specific ODE-parabolic PDE interconnections via coercive Lyapunov functions.
status_evidence.claim: Progress is incremental and limited to specific system classes rather than a general design methodology.
